youtube.title: Tens and Ones for Kids! Place Value at the Bakery | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Cow orders 47 cookies! Robo, Bear and Frog pack them in bakery boxes of ten. Learn tens and ones, count by tens, compare numbers like 35 and 53, and add ten more, at the Tens and Ones Bakery.
For first graders learning place value. Bundle crayons into tens at home and count along!

do.text: Hi Bear, it's Cow! I need 47 cookies for my party.
Can you bring them by lunch?
Forty-seven? How will we ever count them?
Every bakery box holds exactly ten cookies.
Let's fill one. Count with me!
Snap! The tenth cookie closes the lid.
Snap your hands shut like a lid!
Ten or more loose cookies must go in a box.
Ten go in a box. Snap!
Four stay loose. 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones.
Box it up! Ten in a box, and the rest are ones!
I'll count the big pile. By ones!
Oh dear. Frog fell asleep! Let's count with boxes.
Four boxes of ten, and seven loose.
Count the boxes by tens. Then the ones.
47 cookies! Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, and the ones!
Box it up! Clap for each ten: 10, 20, 30, 40!
Yes! Counting by tens is fast.
Let's read tens and ones on our mat.
Boxes go on tens. Loose cookies go on ones.
2 boxes is 2 tens. 3 loose is 3 ones.
The tens digit is 2. The ones digit is 3.
Now 60. Six boxes, and... no loose cookies!
The zero says: no loose cookies.
No, Robo! One box is ten, not one!
Fun fact: we write every number with just ten digits.
Zero, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight and nine!
Digit also means a finger or toe. Wiggle your digits!
53! More boxes wins. Look at the tens first.
Remember: look at the tens digit first.
If the tens are the same, then look at the ones.
Bear, it's Cow again. Ten more cookies, please!
Ten more? That's one more box!
Only the tens digit changed. The ones digit stays 7.
Ten more than 70? Just add one box.
Question one. 5 boxes and 2 loose. How many?
Question two. 68 is how many tens and ones?
Question three. Which is more, 29 or 92?
Five out of five. Great baking!
I'll count. By tens this time!
Fun fact: a baker's dozen is 13, not 12!
Boxes are tens, loose ones are ones. Count the boxes first!
